full_judgment: 3. The properties described in schedule Ka to Uma in the plaint was originally owned and possessed by Jamarat Ali, who by registered deed of heba-bil-ewaz transferred the entire land in favour of his 1st son Rausan Ali in the year 1938, vide, Ext. 1. Jamarat Ali died leaving his son Roushan Ali by his 1st wife and two other sons namely Azibar Ali and Akbar Ali by his second wife. Thereafter Roushan Ali transferred 4.20 acres of land out of the land of the heba-bil-ewaz in favour of his step brothers namely Azibar Ali and Akbar Ali. Thereafter Roushan Ali died leaving widow plaintiff No. 2, a son, plaintiff No. 1 and 2 daughter's plaintiff Nos. 3 and 4. Thereafter Azibar Ali died leaving mother (since dead), full brother defendant No.7 and two sister's defendant Nos. 8 and 9. It is the further case of the plaintiff that the sale deed executed and registered by Roushan Ali in favour of his step-brothers Azibar Ali and Akbar Ali Vide Ext. 'A' is an inactive and inoperative document inasmuch as no consideration money passed and as such the sale deed Ext. 'A' was not acted upon and that Roushan Ali continued to remain in possession of the entire land. It is further stated in the plaint that 1.28 acre of land described in schedule 'Cha' to the plaint out of the entire land of Roushan Ali had wrongly been recorded in the name of the defendants in rent roll khatian and taking advantage of the wrong entry in Rent Roll Khatian defendant threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession from said 1.28 acre of land and hence the suit for confirmation of possession on declaration of title thereto. It is further stated that entry in respect of 1.28 acre of land in SA Khatian is without basis and as such it cannot be allowed to stand. Defendant Nos. 1-6 contested the suit by filing written statement.
